tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

**Goal:** Turn user intent into a hardened, reviewable artifact.

**CRITICAL:** If a step directs you to another snapshot file, read it fully and follow it. No exceptions.

Subagents, when the capability is available, are an important part of this workflow. Use them as directed by the workflow steps.
If you need an explicit user instruction to run them, ask once now for the whole workflow run.

## READY FOR DEVELOPMENT STANDARD

A specification is "Ready for Development" when:

- **Actionable**: Every task has a file path and specific action.
- **Logical**: Tasks ordered by dependency.
- **Testable**: All ACs use Given/When/Then.
- **Complete**: No placeholders or TBDs.
- **Sufficient**: No known requirement, acceptance, dependency, or implementation gaps remain unresolved.
- **Coherent**: No unresolved ambiguities or internal contradictions.

## SCOPE STANDARD

A specification should target a **single user-facing goal** within **900–1600 tokens**:

- **Single goal**: One cohesive feature, even if it spans multiple layers/files. Multi-goal means >=2 **top-level independent shippable deliverables** — each could be reviewed, tested, and merged as a separate PR without breaking the others. Never count surface verbs, "and" conjunctions, or noun phrases. Never split cross-layer implementation details inside one user goal.
  - Split: "add dark mode toggle AND refactor auth to JWT AND build admin dashboard"
  - Don't split: "add validation and display errors" / "support drag-and-drop AND paste AND retry"
- **900–1600 tokens**: Optimal range for LLM consumption. Below 900 risks ambiguity; above 1600 risks context-rot in implementation agents.
- **Neither limit is a gate.** Both are proposals with user override.

## Conventions

- Every operational cross-file reference in this workflow is an absolute snapshot path. Open it directly; do not resolve it relative to a skill directory.
- `{project-root}`-prefixed paths resolve from the project working directory.

1	# Epic 1 Context: Foundation & Session Management
2	
3	<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	This epic delivers the scaffold every other feature depends on: the pinned-stack project setup with its core infrastructure verified working together, the full visual design-token system, email/password authentication with silent session refresh, the session-expiry recovery overlay, and a base navigation shell with placeholders for everything not yet built. It is delivered first because every later epic assumes this foundation — DI, networking, error handling, session state, design tokens, and navigation — already exists and is stable. Users come away able to create an account, log in, stay logged in across restarts, recover gracefully if their session expires mid-use, and navigate the whole app shell even though most feature screens are still placeholders.
8	
9	## Stories
10	
11	- Story 1.1: Project Scaffold, Stack Integration & Core Infrastructure
12	- Story 1.2: Design Token System & Core Component Library
13	- Story 1.3: Account Creation and Login
14	- Story 1.4: Silent Session Refresh & Persistence
15	- Story 1.5: Expired-Session Recovery Overlay
16	- Story 1.6: Base Navigation Shell with Feature Placeholders
17	
18	## Requirements & Constraints
19	
20	- Account creation and login round-trip through the backend with exactly two fields (email, password) — no password confirmation, no display-name field at signup. Login/signup/refresh are the only calls using the anon key; every other call uses the user's access token.
21	- A valid, unexpired session must persist across app restarts with no re-prompt; nearing/past-expiry sessions refresh silently with no visible loading UI unless the call exceeds 300ms.
22	- When the backend reports an expired session, an overlay appears over whatever screen is active (never a navigation away); the underlying screen's state/scroll position is preserved; "Entrar novamente" leads to biometric/PIN re-auth, not a login form.
23	- All four base destinations (Home/Chat, side menu, Meus Registros, Configurações) must be reachable from launch; any destination whose feature isn't built yet shows a visually distinct, fully-polished placeholder — never a broken link and never a visibly "unfinished" look.
24	- Local UI interactions must respond in <100ms; any network call >300ms shows a loading indicator (manual timing spot-check, no automated perf tooling).
25	- Zero Clean Architecture layer violations: domain imports neither Flutter nor anything from a data layer.
26	- ≥80% domain-layer test coverage; the write-failure matrix (5 write endpoints × 3 failure types: timeout, malformed response, no connection = 15 scenarios) must be fully handled with zero unhandled exceptions — this epic builds the one shared, reusable test helper every later feature's write-endpoint tests reuse.
27	- Zero hardcoded visual values outside the design-tokens file; every control must honor Dynamic Type without truncating.
28	- An integration spike, before any other building, must prove `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` work together in one bootstrap — this combination is otherwise unverified.
29	
30	## Technical Decisions
31	
32	- Single DI container: exactly one `get_it` instance registered at bootstrap; `dio` is configured through it; secrets (`FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) load via `flutter_dotenv` from a gitignored `.env`, never hardcoded.
33	- One sealed `Failure` hierarchy, exactly 14 subtypes (13 from the backend's error taxonomy plus a local-only `MalformedResponse`), defined once and never redefined/subset per feature; every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or a `Stream` for SSE), with no native/dio exception ever escaping unmapped.
34	- One retry interceptor on the `dio`/`ApiClient` layer retries only the 6 server-marked `retryable:true` codes; every other failure surfaces once, unretried.
35	- One URL builder maps every operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>` (never the literal OpenAPI REST path); one interceptor owns headers — `apikey` on every call, anon-key bearer token only on signup/login/refresh, user access token on everything else.
36	- Exactly one `SessionStatus` stream is exposed from the auth feature's domain layer and registered once in DI as a singleton; every later consumer (including RF07/Epic 4) injects/listens to it rather than re-deriving session validity from a raw 401 or a second stream.
37	- This epic builds the `go_router` redirect skeleton composing session state; Epic 2 (RF03) later plugs a local vault-status gate into the same redirect, checked before session status — this epic should leave that composition point open rather than hardcoding a session-only redirect.
38	- Strict layer direction applies project-wide: only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins; `presentation/` never imports any feature's `data/` directly; a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency.
39	- Structural seed to scaffold: `lib/core/{design_tokens.dart, network/, failure/, di/, cache/, resource.dart, isolated_side_effect.dart, session/}` and `lib/features/{auth, vault, entries, capture, chat, export, dashboard, account}/`, each pre-wired for `data/domain/presentation`.
40	- Full stack is pinned (Flutter 3.47.x via `fvm`; `flutter_bloc`, `go_router`, `dio`, `hive_ce`, `get_it`, `fpdart`, `freezed`, `json_serializable`, `mocktail`, `fl_chart`, `local_auth`, `flutter_secure_storage`, `flutter_dotenv`, `whisper_ggml` — exact versions in the architecture spine's stack-pins table) and must resolve with no conflicts before anything else is built.
41	- Design tokens (`colors`, `typography`, `rounded`, `spacing`, `components`, plus the two elevation constants) are implemented verbatim, camelCase, as the single source of truth; every other file reads from them, never redefines a value.
42	
43	## UX & Interaction Patterns
44	
45	- Single fixed frame: 390×844 logical points, portrait only, light mode only — no breakpoint, landscape, or dark-mode path anywhere in the app.
46	- Buttons and text fields come from one shared component set: disabled buttons always render `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary` text (never dimmed opacity); text fields show distinct default/focused(`colorPrimary`, 1.5px)/error(`colorError`) border states.
47	- The side menu is the sole navigation hub (plus back arrows and sheet "x" closes) — no drawer-within-drawer, no tab bar. It must resolve all four destinations (chat session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, Planos de Ação) without a 404 or crash.
48	- The Planos de Ação placeholder (an explicit, never-implemented extension feature) must still look fully finished — same visual polish as real screens, no graying-out, no backend calls, no drag/drop logic.
49	- The avatar component (solid `colorPrimary` circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, 40px) is built here for reuse, not reimplementation, when Configurações needs its 52px variant later (Epic 8).
50	- The "Sessão expirada" overlay is a scrim over the current screen using the confirmation-dialog component with a neutral (`colorTextPrimary`) title — never the red destructive-title variant. It traps focus until dismissed/actioned, is the only overlay allowed on screen at a time (never stacks on another open overlay), and its entrance uses only the `scrimIn` (0.18s) choreography — no other motion exists in the system besides `sheetUp` for bottom sheets.
51	- Copy for the overlay must avoid any language implying data loss or starting over; history and scroll position are understood by the user to be preserved.
52	
53	## Cross-Story Dependencies
54	
55	- Story 1.1 (DI, API client, Failure hierarchy, URL builder, retry interceptor, shared failure-matrix test helper) is a hard prerequisite for every other story in this epic and for every later epic's write-endpoint tests.
56	- Story 1.2's design tokens and base components (buttons, text fields, avatar) are consumed by Story 1.3's login/signup screen, Story 1.5's overlay, and Story 1.6's navigation shell/placeholders.
57	- Story 1.4 depends on Story 1.3's auth calls and exposes the singleton `SessionStatus` stream that Story 1.5 listens to and that the `go_router` redirect skeleton composes.
58	- Story 1.5's "Entrar novamente" action routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow that is not built until Epic 2 — this epic should wire the route target without implementing that flow.
59	- Story 1.6's `go_router` redirect skeleton is extended by Epic 2 (RF03), which plugs in the local vault-status gate ahead of the session gate already built here, in a fixed order (vault checked first).
60	- Story 1.6's avatar component and placeholder-styling pattern are reused as-is by Epic 8 (Configurações' 52px avatar, other placeholder surfaces).

# Epic 1 Context: Foundation & Session Management

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

This epic delivers the scaffold every other feature depends on: the pinned-stack project setup with its core infrastructure verified working together, the full visual design-token system, email/password authentication with silent session refresh, the session-expiry recovery overlay, and a base navigation shell with placeholders for everything not yet built. It is delivered first because every later epic assumes this foundation — DI, networking, error handling, session state, design tokens, and navigation — already exists and is stable. Users come away able to create an account, log in, stay logged in across restarts, recover gracefully if their session expires mid-use, and navigate the whole app shell even though most feature screens are still placeholders.

## Stories

- Story 1.1: Project Scaffold, Stack Integration & Core Infrastructure
- Story 1.2: Design Token System & Core Component Library
- Story 1.3: Account Creation and Login
- Story 1.4: Silent Session Refresh & Persistence
- Story 1.5: Expired-Session Recovery Overlay
- Story 1.6: Base Navigation Shell with Feature Placeholders

## Requirements & Constraints

- Account creation and login round-trip through the backend with exactly two fields (email, password) — no password confirmation, no display-name field at signup. Login/signup/refresh are the only calls using the anon key; every other call uses the user's access token.
- A valid, unexpired session must persist across app restarts with no re-prompt; nearing/past-expiry sessions refresh silently with no visible loading UI unless the call exceeds 300ms.
- When the backend reports an expired session, an overlay appears over whatever screen is active (never a navigation away); the underlying screen's state/scroll position is preserved; "Entrar novamente" leads to biometric/PIN re-auth, not a login form.
- All four base destinations (Home/Chat, side menu, Meus Registros, Configurações) must be reachable from launch; any destination whose feature isn't built yet shows a visually distinct, fully-polished placeholder — never a broken link and never a visibly "unfinished" look.
- Local UI interactions must respond in <100ms; any network call >300ms shows a loading indicator (manual timing spot-check, no automated perf tooling).
- Zero Clean Architecture layer violations: domain imports neither Flutter nor anything from a data layer.
- ≥80% domain-layer test coverage; the write-failure matrix (5 write endpoints × 3 failure types: timeout, malformed response, no connection = 15 scenarios) must be fully handled with zero unhandled exceptions — this epic builds the one shared, reusable test helper every later feature's write-endpoint tests reuse.
- Zero hardcoded visual values outside the design-tokens file; every control must honor Dynamic Type without truncating.
- An integration spike, before any other building, must prove `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` work together in one bootstrap — this combination is otherwise unverified.

## Technical Decisions

- Single DI container: exactly one `get_it` instance registered at bootstrap; `dio` is configured through it; secrets (`FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) load via `flutter_dotenv` from a gitignored `.env`, never hardcoded.
- One sealed `Failure` hierarchy, exactly 14 subtypes (13 from the backend's error taxonomy plus a local-only `MalformedResponse`), defined once and never redefined/subset per feature; every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or a `Stream` for SSE), with no native/dio exception ever escaping unmapped.
- One retry interceptor on the `dio`/`ApiClient` layer retries only the 6 server-marked `retryable:true` codes; every other failure surfaces once, unretried.
- One URL builder maps every operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>` (never the literal OpenAPI REST path); one interceptor owns headers — `apikey` on every call, anon-key bearer token only on signup/login/refresh, user access token on everything else.
- Exactly one `SessionStatus` stream is exposed from the auth feature's domain layer and registered once in DI as a singleton; every later consumer (including RF07/Epic 4) injects/listens to it rather than re-deriving session validity from a raw 401 or a second stream.
- This epic builds the `go_router` redirect skeleton composing session state; Epic 2 (RF03) later plugs a local vault-status gate into the same redirect, checked before session status — this epic should leave that composition point open rather than hardcoding a session-only redirect.
- Strict layer direction applies project-wide: only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins; `presentation/` never imports any feature's `data/` directly; a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency.
- Structural seed to scaffold: `lib/core/{design_tokens.dart, network/, failure/, di/, cache/, resource.dart, isolated_side_effect.dart, session/}` and `lib/features/{auth, vault, entries, capture, chat, export, dashboard, account}/`, each pre-wired for `data/domain/presentation`.
- Full stack is pinned (Flutter 3.47.x via `fvm`; `flutter_bloc`, `go_router`, `dio`, `hive_ce`, `get_it`, `fpdart`, `freezed`, `json_serializable`, `mocktail`, `fl_chart`, `local_auth`, `flutter_secure_storage`, `flutter_dotenv`, `whisper_ggml` — exact versions in the architecture spine's stack-pins table) and must resolve with no conflicts before anything else is built.
- Design tokens (`colors`, `typography`, `rounded`, `spacing`, `components`, plus the two elevation constants) are implemented verbatim, camelCase, as the single source of truth; every other file reads from them, never redefines a value.

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- Single fixed frame: 390×844 logical points, portrait only, light mode only — no breakpoint, landscape, or dark-mode path anywhere in the app.
- Buttons and text fields come from one shared component set: disabled buttons always render `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary` text (never dimmed opacity); text fields show distinct default/focused(`colorPrimary`, 1.5px)/error(`colorError`) border states.
- The side menu is the sole navigation hub (plus back arrows and sheet "x" closes) — no drawer-within-drawer, no tab bar. It must resolve all four destinations (chat session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, Planos de Ação) without a 404 or crash.
- The Planos de Ação placeholder (an explicit, never-implemented extension feature) must still look fully finished — same visual polish as real screens, no graying-out, no backend calls, no drag/drop logic.
- The avatar component (solid `colorPrimary` circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, 40px) is built here for reuse, not reimplementation, when Configurações needs its 52px variant later (Epic 8).
- The "Sessão expirada" overlay is a scrim over the current screen using the confirmation-dialog component with a neutral (`colorTextPrimary`) title — never the red destructive-title variant. It traps focus until dismissed/actioned, is the only overlay allowed on screen at a time (never stacks on another open overlay), and its entrance uses only the `scrimIn` (0.18s) choreography — no other motion exists in the system besides `sheetUp` for bottom sheets.
- Copy for the overlay must avoid any language implying data loss or starting over; history and scroll position are understood by the user to be preserved.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Story 1.1 (DI, API client, Failure hierarchy, URL builder, retry interceptor, shared failure-matrix test helper) is a hard prerequisite for every other story in this epic and for every later epic's write-endpoint tests.
- Story 1.2's design tokens and base components (buttons, text fields, avatar) are consumed by Story 1.3's login/signup screen, Story 1.5's overlay, and Story 1.6's navigation shell/placeholders.
- Story 1.4 depends on Story 1.3's auth calls and exposes the singleton `SessionStatus` stream that Story 1.5 listens to and that the `go_router` redirect skeleton composes.
- Story 1.5's "Entrar novamente" action routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow that is not built until Epic 2 — this epic should wire the route target without implementing that flow.
- Story 1.6's `go_router` redirect skeleton is extended by Epic 2 (RF03), which plugs in the local vault-status gate ahead of the session gate already built here, in a fixed order (vault checked first).
- Story 1.6's avatar component and placeholder-styling pattern are reused as-is by Epic 8 (Configurações' 52px avatar, other placeholder surfaces).

2	title: 'Story 1.4: Silent Session Refresh & Persistence'
3	type: 'feature'
4	created: '2026-10-27'
5	status: 'done'
6	review_loop_iteration: 0
7	baseline_commit: '8a4b94403d05281d58068aa4dac46dc08adf1873'
8	context:

12	---
13	
14	<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">
15	
16	## Intent
17	
18	**Problem:** `AccessTokenProvider` only persists the access token (`access_token_provider.dart:8-35`); the refresh token already decoded into `AuthResponseDto` is discarded (`auth_repository_impl.dart:63-65`), and `main.dart` hardcodes `AuthScreen` as home with zero bootstrap check (`main.dart:36-46`) — so a valid session never survives a restart.
19	
20	**Approach:** Persist the refresh token; add a `SessionRepository` in the auth domain that, on launch, unconditionally exchanges any stored refresh token for a fresh pair via `auth-refresh`, exposing the result as the epic's one singleton `SessionStatus` stream. `main.dart` branches its `home` on that stream's first emission instead of hardcoding `AuthScreen`.
21	
22	## Boundaries & Constraints
23	
24	**Always:**
25	- Boot calls `auth-refresh` once, unconditionally, whenever a refresh token is stored — no client-side expiry math or clock comparison; the server is the sole source of truth for validity.
26	- `AccessTokenProvider` gains `saveSession({accessToken, refreshToken})`, `readRefreshToken()`, `clearSession()`; existing `readAccessToken`/`saveAccessToken`/`clearAccessToken` stay untouched for `HeaderInterceptor` (`access_token_provider.dart:8-14`).
27	- `auth-refresh` stays in `HeaderInterceptor.anonKeyOnlyFunctions` (`header_interceptor.dart:20-24`) — refresh must never need the (possibly dead) access-token bearer.
28	- `SessionRepository.statusStream`/`restoreSession()` is the ONE new DI-singleton access point for session validity (epic AD) — no second stream, no raw-401 re-derivation.
29	- `AuthRepositoryImpl._authenticate` (`auth_repository_impl.dart:46-74`) persists the refresh token returned by signup/login too, via the same `saveSession`.
30	- A dead/missing refresh token reuses the closed 14-subtype `Failure` hierarchy (`AuthExpired`/`AuthInvalid`) — no new subtype (`failure.dart`).
31	
32	**Ask First:** if the backend's `auth-refresh` response omits any field `openapi.yaml:197-234` marks required, HALT before guessing a fallback.
33	
34	**Never:**
35	- No reactive refresh-and-retry-on-401 interceptor — mid-session expiry while the app is running is Story 1.5's overlay scope, not this story's.
36	- No `go_router` wiring (Story 1.6) — `main.dart` keeps its current `MaterialApp`/`Navigator` shape; only `home` changes.
37	- No new Cubit for this story — `main.dart` drives directly off `SessionRepository`.
38	
39	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
40	
41	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
42	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
43	| Cold boot, valid refresh token | refreshToken stored, backend accepts | `auth-refresh` succeeds, new pair saved, stream emits `authenticated`, home = post-auth placeholder | N/A |
44	| Cold boot, no stored session | no refresh token (fresh install / post-logout) | no network call, stream emits `unauthenticated` immediately, home = `AuthScreen` | N/A |
45	| Cold boot, dead refresh token | refreshToken stored, backend returns `AUTH_EXPIRED`/`AUTH_INVALID` | session cleared, stream emits `unauthenticated`, home = `AuthScreen` | silent — no error UI |
46	| Cold boot, offline | refreshToken stored, no connectivity | stream emits `unauthenticated` (fail-closed), storage left untouched | silent; next boot retries naturally |
47	| Successful signup/login (1.3 path) | — | refresh token now also saved via `saveSession` | N/A |
48	
49	</frozen-after-approval>
50	
51	## Code Map
52	
53	- `lib/core/network/access_token_provider.dart:8-35` -- add `saveSession`/`readRefreshToken`/`clearSession` to the abstract port + the `FlutterSecureStorage` impl (new key alongside existing `_key`).
54	- `lib/features/auth/data/models/auth_response_dto.dart` -- `AuthSessionDto` already decodes `refreshToken`; reuse as-is, no DTO change.
55	- `lib/features/auth/data/datasources/auth_remote_data_source.dart:12-47` -- add `refresh(String refreshToken)`, posting `{refreshToken}` to `auth-refresh` (own body shape, can't reuse the email/password `_post` helper as-is).
56	- `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/auth_repository_impl.dart:46-74` -- `_authenticate` calls `saveSession(...)` instead of `saveAccessToken` only.
57	- `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart` -- new: `enum SessionStatus { authenticated, unauthenticated }`.
58	- `lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart` -- new: `Stream<SessionStatus> get statusStream; Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> restoreSession();`.
59	- `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart` -- new: owns the broadcast `StreamController`, calls `AuthRemoteDataSource.refresh`, persists/clears via `AccessTokenProvider`.
60	- `lib/features/auth/auth_injection.dart:13-24` -- register `SessionRepository` singleton (after `AccessTokenProvider`/`AuthRemoteDataSource`).
61	- `lib/main.dart:23-67` -- `CerneApp` calls `sl<SessionRepository>().restoreSession()` once, branches `home` on a `StreamBuilder<SessionStatus>` (no-data yet = brief blank, per RNF01's 300ms threshold) between `AuthScreen` and the existing `_PostAuthPlaceholder`.
62	- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:179-240` -- `auth-refresh` ground truth: `{refreshToken}` in, same `session` shape out, `security: []`.
63	
64	## Tasks & Acceptance
65	
66	**Execution:**
67	- [x] `access_token_provider.dart` -- add `saveSession`/`readRefreshToken`/`clearSession` -- new secure-storage surface for the refresh token
68	- [x] `auth_remote_data_source.dart` -- add `refresh()` -- calls `auth-refresh` per contract
69	- [x] `auth_repository_impl.dart` -- `_authenticate` persists the refresh token too -- closes the gap 1.3 flagged
70	- [x] `session_status.dart` -- new enum -- the two-state status the epic's AD requires
71	- [x] `session_repository.dart` (domain) + `session_repository_impl.dart` (data) -- new -- singleton stream + boot-time restore
72	- [x] `auth_injection.dart` -- register `SessionRepository` -- DI wiring
73	- [x] `main.dart` -- boot-time `restoreSession()` + `StreamBuilder` home branch -- replaces the hardcoded `AuthScreen` home
74	- [x] `test/.../session_repository_impl_test.dart` -- cover the I/O matrix rows (valid/none/dead/offline) with `mocktail`
75	- [x] `test/.../auth_remote_data_source_test.dart` -- `refresh()` write-failure matrix (timeout/malformed/offline) per RNF09
76	- [x] `test/main_test.dart` -- extend for both boot branches (authenticated vs unauthenticated home)
77	
78	**Acceptance Criteria:**
79	- Given a stored refresh token the backend accepts, when the app launches, then the user reaches the authenticated placeholder with no login prompt and no visible loading UI in the happy path (<300ms).
80	- Given no stored session or a refresh token the backend rejects, when the app launches, then the user lands on `AuthScreen` with no error message shown.
81	- Given a successful signup/login, when `AuthRepositoryImpl` returns, then both the access token and refresh token are persisted, unchanged `Either<Failure,T>` signature (RNF09).
82	
83	### Review Findings
84	
85	- [x] [Review][Patch] `_asUnauthenticated`'s comment overstates what `restoreSession()`'s `catchError` "insurance" (`main.dart:54-75`) actually does — it suppresses an unhandled zone exception, but since the whole call is `unawaited`, its return value is discarded and never reaches `statusStream`; it does NOT unblock the UI from `_BootLoadingScreen`. Today this is unreachable dead code (every repository method in this diff returns `Either` and never throws), and fixing the underlying gap for real would mean widening the frozen `SessionRepository` interface ("the ONE new DI-singleton access point... no second stream") for a path with no current trigger — not worth renegotiating the frozen spec for. Fix: reword the comment to say it only prevents an unhandled zone exception, not that it recovers the UI. [lib/main.dart:69-75]
86	- [x] [Review][Patch] `statusStream` getter returns a new `Stream.multi` instance on every access; `main.dart` passes it directly into `StreamBuilder` instead of caching it — currently inert because `_CerneAppState.build()` only runs once (no `setState`, no `InheritedWidget` dependency), but it's a latent resubscription/flash-to-boot-screen bug waiting for any future rebuild trigger. Fix: cache `late final Stream<SessionStatus> _statusStream = _sessionRepository.statusStream;` once in `_CerneAppState` and reference that field in `build()`. [lib/main.dart:82]
87	- [x] [Review][Patch] No `isClosed` guard before `_statusController.add()` in `_emit()`; `dispose()` closes that same controller. If `dispose()` (wired to `get_it`'s `sl.reset()`) ever runs while a `restoreSession()` call is still in flight, the pending `.add()` throws an unhandled `StateError` — not exercised by any current test, but a real race the moment DI is torn down with a boot restore still pending (dev hot-restart, a future logout-reset flow). Fix: guard `_emit()` with `if (!_statusController.isClosed) { ... }`. [lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart:68]
88	- [x] [Review][Patch] `_BootLoadingScreen`'s 300ms blank→spinner `Timer` logic has zero test coverage — explicitly called out by the spec as this story's own new UI (the reason RNF01's verification grep was widened to `lib/main.dart`), but every `main_test.dart` boot test uses `pumpAndSettle()`, which fast-forwards past the internal `Timer`. Neither "stays blank below 300ms" nor "shows spinner past 300ms" is ever asserted. type: 'feature'
created: '2026-10-27'

  - '{project-root}/docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** `AccessTokenProvider` only persists the access token (`access_token_provider.dart:8-35`); the refresh token already decoded into `AuthResponseDto` is discarded (`auth_repository_impl.dart:63-65`), and `main.dart` hardcodes `AuthScreen` as home with zero bootstrap check (`main.dart:36-46`) — so a valid session never survives a restart.

**Approach:** Persist the refresh token; add a `SessionRepository` in the auth domain that, on launch, unconditionally exchanges any stored refresh token for a fresh pair via `auth-refresh`, exposing the result as the epic's one singleton `SessionStatus` stream. `main.dart` branches its `home` on that stream's first emission instead of hardcoding `AuthScreen`.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Boot calls `auth-refresh` once, unconditionally, whenever a refresh token is stored — no client-side expiry math or clock comparison; the server is the sole source of truth for validity.
- `AccessTokenProvider` gains `saveSession({accessToken, refreshToken})`, `readRefreshToken()`, `clearSession()`; existing `readAccessToken`/`saveAccessToken`/`clearAccessToken` stay untouched for `HeaderInterceptor` (`access_token_provider.dart:8-14`).
- `auth-refresh` stays in `HeaderInterceptor.anonKeyOnlyFunctions` (`header_interceptor.dart:20-24`) — refresh must never need the (possibly dead) access-token bearer.
- `SessionRepository.statusStream`/`restoreSession()` is the ONE new DI-singleton access point for session validity (epic AD) — no second stream, no raw-401 re-derivation.
- `AuthRepositoryImpl._authenticate` (`auth_repository_impl.dart:46-74`) persists the refresh token returned by signup/login too, via the same `saveSession`.
- A dead/missing refresh token reuses the closed 14-subtype `Failure` hierarchy (`AuthExpired`/`AuthInvalid`) — no new subtype (`failure.dart`).

**Ask First:** if the backend's `auth-refresh` response omits any field `openapi.yaml:197-234` marks required, HALT before guessing a fallback.

**Never:**
- No reactive refresh-and-retry-on-401 interceptor — mid-session expiry while the app is running is Story 1.5's overlay scope, not this story's.
- No `go_router` wiring (Story 1.6) — `main.dart` keeps its current `MaterialApp`/`Navigator` shape; only `home` changes.
- No new Cubit for this story — `main.dart` drives directly off `SessionRepository`.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Cold boot, valid refresh token | refreshToken stored, backend accepts | `auth-refresh` succeeds, new pair saved, stream emits `authenticated`, home = post-auth placeholder | N/A |
| Cold boot, no stored session | no refresh token (fresh install / post-logout) | no network call, stream emits `unauthenticated` immediately, home = `AuthScreen` | N/A |
| Cold boot, dead refresh token | refreshToken stored, backend returns `AUTH_EXPIRED`/`AUTH_INVALID` | session cleared, stream emits `unauthenticated`, home = `AuthScreen` | silent — no error UI |
| Cold boot, offline | refreshToken stored, no connectivity | stream emits `unauthenticated` (fail-closed), storage left untouched | silent; next boot retries naturally |
| Successful signup/login (1.3 path) | — | refresh token now also saved via `saveSession` | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/core/network/access_token_provider.dart:8-35` -- add `saveSession`/`readRefreshToken`/`clearSession` to the abstract port + the `FlutterSecureStorage` impl (new key alongside existing `_key`).
- `lib/features/auth/data/models/auth_response_dto.dart` -- `AuthSessionDto` already decodes `refreshToken`; reuse as-is, no DTO change.
- `lib/features/auth/data/datasources/auth_remote_data_source.dart:12-47` -- add `refresh(String refreshToken)`, posting `{refreshToken}` to `auth-refresh` (own body shape, can't reuse the email/password `_post` helper as-is).
- `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/auth_repository_impl.dart:46-74` -- `_authenticate` calls `saveSession(...)` instead of `saveAccessToken` only.
- `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart` -- new: `enum SessionStatus { authenticated, unauthenticated }`.
- `lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart` -- new: `Stream<SessionStatus> get statusStream; Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> restoreSession();`.
- `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart` -- new: owns the broadcast `StreamController`, calls `AuthRemoteDataSource.refresh`, persists/clears via `AccessTokenProvider`.
- `lib/features/auth/auth_injection.dart:13-24` -- register `SessionRepository` singleton (after `AccessTokenProvider`/`AuthRemoteDataSource`).
- `lib/main.dart:23-67` -- `CerneApp` calls `sl<SessionRepository>().restoreSession()` once, branches `home` on a `StreamBuilder<SessionStatus>` (no-data yet = brief blank, per RNF01's 300ms threshold) between `AuthScreen` and the existing `_PostAuthPlaceholder`.
- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:179-240` -- `auth-refresh` ground truth: `{refreshToken}` in, same `session` shape out, `security: []`.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `access_token_provider.dart` -- add `saveSession`/`readRefreshToken`/`clearSession` -- new secure-storage surface for the refresh token
- [x] `auth_remote_data_source.dart` -- add `refresh()` -- calls `auth-refresh` per contract
- [x] `auth_repository_impl.dart` -- `_authenticate` persists the refresh token too -- closes the gap 1.3 flagged
- [x] `session_status.dart` -- new enum -- the two-state status the epic's AD requires
- [x] `session_repository.dart` (domain) + `session_repository_impl.dart` (data) -- new -- singleton stream + boot-time restore
- [x] `auth_injection.dart` -- register `SessionRepository` -- DI wiring
- [x] `main.dart` -- boot-time `restoreSession()` + `StreamBuilder` home branch -- replaces the hardcoded `AuthScreen` home
- [x] `test/.../session_repository_impl_test.dart` -- cover the I/O matrix rows (valid/none/dead/offline) with `mocktail`
- [x] `test/.../auth_remote_data_source_test.dart` -- `refresh()` write-failure matrix (timeout/malformed/offline) per RNF09
- [x] `test/main_test.dart` -- extend for both boot branches (authenticated vs unauthenticated home)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a stored refresh token the backend accepts, when the app launches, then the user reaches the authenticated placeholder with no login prompt and no visible loading UI in the happy path (<300ms).
- Given no stored session or a refresh token the backend rejects, when the app launches, then the user lands on `AuthScreen` with no error message shown.
- Given a successful signup/login, when `AuthRepositoryImpl` returns, then both the access token and refresh token are persisted, unchanged `Either<Failure,T>` signature (RNF09).

- [x] [Review][Patch] `_asUnauthenticated`'s comment overstates what `restoreSession()`'s `catchError` "insurance" (`main.dart:54-75`) actually does — it suppresses an unhandled zone exception, but since the whole call is `unawaited`, its return value is discarded and never reaches `statusStream`; it does NOT unblock the UI from `_BootLoadingScreen`. Today this is unreachable dead code (every repository method in this diff returns `Either` and never throws), and fixing the underlying gap for real would mean widening the frozen `SessionRepository` interface ("the ONE new DI-singleton access point... no second stream") for a path with no current trigger — not worth renegotiating the frozen spec for. Fix: reword the comment to say it only prevents an unhandled zone exception, not that it recovers the UI. [lib/main.dart:69-75]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `statusStream` getter returns a new `Stream.multi` instance on every access; `main.dart` passes it directly into `StreamBuilder` instead of caching it — currently inert because `_CerneAppState.build()` only runs once (no `setState`, no `InheritedWidget` dependency), but it's a latent resubscription/flash-to-boot-screen bug waiting for any future rebuild trigger. Fix: cache `late final Stream<SessionStatus> _statusStream = _sessionRepository.statusStream;` once in `_CerneAppState` and reference that field in `build()`. [lib/main.dart:82]
- [x] [Review][Patch] No `isClosed` guard before `_statusController.add()` in `_emit()`; `dispose()` closes that same controller. If `dispose()` (wired to `get_it`'s `sl.reset()`) ever runs while a `restoreSession()` call is still in flight, the pending `.add()` throws an unhandled `StateError` — not exercised by any current test, but a real race the moment DI is torn down with a boot restore still pending (dev hot-restart, a future logout-reset flow). Fix: guard `_emit()` with `if (!_statusController.isClosed) { ... }`. [lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart:68]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `_BootLoadingScreen`'s 300ms blank→spinner `Timer` logic has zero test coverage — explicitly called out by the spec as this story's own new UI (the reason RNF01's verification grep was widened to `lib/main.dart`), but every `main_test.dart` boot test uses `pumpAndSettle()`, which fast-forwards past the internal `Timer`. Neither "stays blank below 300ms" nor "shows spinner past 300ms" is ever asserted. Fix: add a widget test using `tester.pump(duration)` (not `pumpAndSettle`) to assert the blank state before 300ms and the spinner after. [lib/main.dart:137]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `readRefreshToken()` returning a non-null empty string isn't treated as "no session" — `restoreSession()` only null-checks the result (`session_repository_impl.dart:86`), so a stored empty-string refresh token (the response schema has no `minLength` on this field) would fire a network call to `auth-refresh` with an empty token (itself `minLength: 1` on the request) instead of short-circuiting like the no-token case. [lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart:86]

Compounding this, `passwordChanged()`'s new symmetric `emailError` clear is reachable through the real `AuthScreen` (malformed-email submit sets `emailError`, then editing only the password field should clear it) and has no regression test in either `auth_cubit_test.dart` or `auth_screen_test.dart` — this one should be fixed now, not deferred, since it's in-scope and the fix is unambiguous. Fix: correct both `deferred-work.md` bullets' "not touched" claim, and add the missing `passwordChanged`-clears-`emailError` test. [lib/features/auth/presentation/cubit/auth_cubit.dart:45]
- [x] [Review][Defer] `AuthCubit.toggleMode()`'s `copyWith`-based status-preservation fix has no regression test that can observe the regression it fixes. Checked reachability: its only call site is a button disabled whenever `isSubmitting` is true, and every failure path resets `status` to idle in the same `emit` as the one that sets `formError` — so there's no path in the current UI that can exercise a non-idle `status` at `toggleMode()` time. Legitimately deferred (unlike the `passwordChanged` item above), but the reason recorded in `deferred-work.md` should say "unreachable via current UI," not "not touched by story 1.4's diff." [lib/features/auth/presentation/cubit/auth_cubit.dart:23] — deferred, pre-existing

- [x] [Review][Patch] No widget-level test drives a backend/network failure while in signup mode — only login mode's failure rendering is covered at the screen level. Fixed — added an `AUTH_INVALID`-in-signup-mode widget test. [test/features/auth/presentation/screens/auth_screen_test.dart]

- **Post-auth destination:** `SessionStatus` (1.4) / `go_router` (1.6) don't exist yet — success swaps `main.dart`'s screen to a small inline placeholder via `Navigator.pushReplacement`, deleted wholesale by Story 1.6.

input.prompt:
In this Flutter repo (cerne-ciclo-b), I need to find what shared UI building blocks already exist for Story 1.5 "Expired-Session Recovery Overlay". The epic context says: "The 'Sessão expirada' overlay is a scrim over the current screen using the confirmation-dialog component with a neutral (colorTextPrimary) title — never the red destructive-title variant. It traps focus until dismissed/actioned, is the only overlay allowed on screen at a time (never stacks on another open overlay), and its entrance uses only the scrimIn (0.18s) choreography — no other motion exists in the system besides sheetUp for bottom sheets."

Please investigate and report back (don't write code, just research):
1. Does a "confirmation-dialog" component already exist in lib/core/widgets/ or lib/core/? Search for dialog, confirmation, modal, alert widgets. Give exact file path and read its full contents if found.
2. Does a "scrim" concept exist anywhere (color token, widget, animation)? Check lib/core/design_tokens.dart for scrim-related tokens, and check docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md for "scrimIn" animation spec (duration, curve, what it animates).
3. Is there any existing overlay/dialog-showing mechanism (e.g. showDialog, showGeneralDialog, a custom overlay manager) anywhere in lib/?
4. What does docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md say about the "Sessão expirada" / session-expired overlay screen specifically — exact copy text, button labels, layout? Search for "expirad" (Portuguese for expired) case-insensitively.
5. What does docs/input/requirements.md say about RF (functional requirement) covering session expiry recovery — find the exact requirement ID, acceptance criteria text, and delivery-order entry for story 1.5. Also check for RNF01 (loading indicator >300ms rule) and any requirement about overlay/focus-trap behavior.
6. Read lib/main.dart in full (current state) — I need to understand current app shell structure (StreamBuilder on SessionStatus, how screens are composed) to know where an overlay would need to be inserted so it appears "over whatever screen is active."
7. Read lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart and lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart in full — current two-state enum authenticated/unauthenticated. Note: Story 1.5 will need the backend's AUTH_EXPIRED signal detected mid-session (not at boot) - check docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md and openapi.yaml for AUTH_EXPIRED code and whether it's "retryable", and check lib/core/network/ (api_client.dart, header_interceptor.dart, any retry interceptor) for how 401/error codes currently get surfaced - is there a central place a mid-session 401 passes through where a new interceptor/listener could detect AUTH_EXPIRED and trigger the overlay?
8. Check lib/core/failure/failure.dart for the full 14-subtype Failure hierarchy and confirm AuthExpired exists as a subtype.
9. Read lib/core/widgets/app_button.dart and lib/core/widgets/avatar.dart in full (small files) so I know their current public API (for potential reuse in the overlay's "Entrar novamente" button).
10. Check lib/core/design_tokens.dart in full for relevant tokens: colorTextPrimary, colorError title variant concept (is there a dialog title color param already?), elevation constants, rounded/spacing tokens relevant to a dialog/card.

Report everything concretely with file:line references and exact quoted text/code where relevant. This is pure research — do not write or edit any files.

13:The prototype has **32 navigable states**, reachable from a single state machine (a `screen` variable plus overlay flags). Not every state is a new full screen — several are **overlays** (modal, sheet, bottom sheet, dialog) shown on top of one of three base screens: **Home/Chat**, **Meus Registros** and **Configurações**. Overlays preserve the screen underneath (it stays visible, with a darkened scrim behind).
69:| Tela 1 — Sessão expirada | Light scrim over the chat (still readable), centered card with lock icon, title "Sessão expirada", text saying history and scroll position are kept, button "Entrar novamente". |
79:| Áudio — Processando | Spinner in place of stop; frozen, faded waveform (opacity .35); text "Transcrevendo..."; label "00:42 de áudio". |
80:| Áudio — Transcrito | Editable transcribed text; original audio duration in mono; "Salvar" enabled. |
174:### Micro-animations and transitions
175:- `scrimIn` (0.18 s ease-out): fade of the darkened background when any overlay opens.
176:- `sheetUp` (0.2 s ease-out): bottom sheets (insertion modal, filter, export) rise from the bottom of the screen.
227:| Confirmation dialog | Sessão expirada, Confirmar exclusão | background scrim + centered card; neutral title (session) or red title (destructive deletion) |

6	/// The epic's ONE new DI-singleton access point for session validity (AD) —
7	/// every later consumer (Story 1.5's overlay, Story 1.6's `go_router`
8	/// redirect, Epic 4/RF07) listens to [statusStream] rather than re-deriving
9	/// session validity from a raw 401 or a second stream (RNF09 — still
10	/// `Either<Failure, T>` for the one-shot [restoreSession] call).
11	abstract class SessionRepository {
12	  /// Broadcast stream of the current session status. Emits nothing until
13	  /// [restoreSession] (or a later story's own trigger) completes at least
14	  /// once — a `StreamBuilder` with no data yet is the brief-blank boot state
15	  /// `main.dart` relies on (RNF01's 300ms threshold).
16	  Stream<SessionStatus> get statusStream;
17	
18	  /// Boot-time, unconditional refresh: exchanges any stored refresh token
19	  /// for a fresh pair via `auth-refresh`, persists the result, and emits the
20	  /// outcome on [statusStream]. No client-side expiry math — the server is
21	  /// the sole source of truth for validity.
22	  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> restoreSession();
23	
24	  /// Releases the underlying stream resource. Wired as `get_it`'s
25	  /// `dispose:` callback on registration, so `resetCoreDependencies()`
26	  /// (`sl.reset()`) closes it instead of leaking a `StreamController` on
27	  /// every test teardown.
28	  Future<void> dispose();
29	}

---
title: 'Story 1.5: Expired-Session Recovery Overlay'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-10-28'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context:
  - '{project-root}/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-1-context.md'
  - '{project-root}/docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md'
  - '{project-root}/docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** `ApiClient._mapDioException` already maps any mid-session `AUTH_EXPIRED` response to `Failure.authExpired` (`api_client.dart:95-111`), but nothing reacts to it — `SessionStatus` only ever emits from the boot-time `restoreSession()` call (`session_repository_impl.dart:81-136`), so an expired session mid-use today surfaces only as a raw inline error on whatever screen made the call, and the user is never routed back to re-auth.

**Approach:** Add a core `SessionExpiryNotifier` port (in the already-scaffolded empty `lib/core/session/`) that `ApiClient` signals on any non-boot `AUTH_EXPIRED`; `SessionRepositoryImpl` bridges that into one new `SessionStatus.expired` value on the epic's existing single stream. `main.dart` keeps rendering the same authenticated screen across that transition and shows a new shared `ConfirmationDialog` overlay (neutral title) whose "Entrar novamente" button routes to a throwaway re-auth placeholder standing in for Epic 2's biometric/PIN flow.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `ApiClient` notifies expiry only for `AUTH_EXPIRED` on calls outside `HeaderInterceptor.anonKeyOnlyFunctions` (`header_interceptor.dart:20-24`, matched via its `functionNameOf`) — boot-time `auth-refresh` keeps going through Story 1.4's existing `restoreSession()` path untouched.
- `SessionStatus` gains exactly one new `expired` value; `statusStream`/`restoreSession`/`dispose` signatures are unchanged — still the epic's one singleton stream (AD), no second stream.
- `SessionRepositoryImpl` emits `expired` only when `_lastStatus == SessionStatus.authenticated`; any other current status ignores the event (no spurious overlay during boot or after logout).
- Overlay = new `ConfirmationDialog` (`lib/core/widgets/`): neutral `colorTextPrimary` title (never `colorError`), non-dismissible barrier, focus-trapped, at most one open at a time (UX-DR16/25/27/36). Entrance is exactly `scrimIn` (0.18s ease-out fade) — the system's only other animation, `sheetUp`, is untouched.
- The authenticated screen's widget instance is never replaced across `authenticated`↔`expired` transitions — scroll/state preserved; the `AuthScreen` branch is unaffected.
- Copy never implies data loss; must state history/scroll position are preserved (mirrors the prototype's own "Sessão expirada" copy).

**Ask First:** if a future consumer needs a session state beyond this story's single new `expired` value, HALT before adding a fourth `SessionStatus` member — renegotiate the epic's AD first.

**Never:**
- No `go_router` — `main.dart` keeps its current `MaterialApp`/`Navigator` shape (Story 1.6).
- No Epic 2 biometric/PIN implementation — "Entrar novamente" only navigates to a throwaway placeholder that Epic 2 deletes wholesale.
- No new icon-font dependency — approximate the prototype's `ph-lock-key` with a built-in Material icon.
- No Reduce-Motion handling — out of this epic's scope.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Mid-session expiry | authenticated, any screen, any endpoint returns `AUTH_EXPIRED` | overlay appears over the current screen; its scroll/state is preserved | silent — no extra inline error |
| Already-open overlay | a second `AUTH_EXPIRED` arrives while the dialog is showing | no second dialog stacks | silent, single-overlay guard holds |
| Expiry while not authenticated | notifier fires but `_lastStatus != authenticated` (e.g. post-logout race) | no emission, no overlay | silent no-op |
| Boot-time refresh expiry | `restoreSession()`'s own `auth-refresh` call returns `AUTH_EXPIRED` | unchanged Story 1.4 behavior — lands on `AuthScreen`, never the overlay | existing path, untouched |
| "Entrar novamente" tapped | overlay visible | dialog dismissed, user routed to the biometric/PIN placeholder | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/core/session/session_expiry_notifier.dart` -- new: `SessionExpiryNotifier` port + broadcast-stream impl, pure Dart (no Flutter/feature import, RNF06) — the directory exists today as a Story 1.1 scaffold (`.gitkeep` only).
- `lib/core/network/api_client.dart:95-111` -- `_mapDioException` additionally calls `SessionExpiryNotifier.notifyExpired()` when the mapped failure `is AuthExpired` and `HeaderInterceptor.functionNameOf(e.requestOptions.path)` isn't in `anonKeyOnlyFunctions` (`header_interceptor.dart:20-24,80-83`) — new constructor dependency.
- `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart:33-61` -- register `SessionExpiryNotifier` as a singleton (with `dispose:`) before `ApiClient`; pass it into `ApiClient`'s constructor.
- `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart` -- add third value `expired` to the current 2-value enum.
- `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart:27-140` -- constructor takes `SessionExpiryNotifier`; subscribes to `expiredEvents`, emits `SessionStatus.expired` per the "Always" guard above; cancels the subscription in `dispose()` (`:139`).
- `lib/features/auth/auth_injection.dart:33-39` -- pass `sessionExpiryNotifier: sl<SessionExpiryNotifier>()` into `SessionRepositoryImpl`.
- `lib/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog.dart` -- new shared component (UX-DR16): scrim + centered card, `titleColor` param (neutral here; Epic 8's account-deletion dialog later passes `colorError`), non-dismissible barrier, single-overlay guard, `scrimIn` entrance.
- `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` -- add `colorScrim` (see Design Notes) plus any new named spacing/padding constants the dialog card needs beyond the existing scale (RNF08).
- `lib/main.dart:90-132` -- `StreamBuilder` treats `authenticated`/`expired` as the same `_PostAuthPlaceholder` render; a small listener shows/dismisses `ConfirmationDialog` on that transition; new throwaway `_BiometricReauthPlaceholder` (same pattern as `_PostAuthPlaceholder`) is "Entrar novamente"'s target.
- Ground truth for copy/visuals: `docs/input/prototype/cerne-prototype.html` ("OVERLAY: Sessão expirada" block) and `prototype-extract.md:69,174-176,227`; `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md:7` (`AUTH_EXPIRED`, 401, non-retryable).

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `lib/core/session/session_expiry_notifier.dart` -- new port + impl -- lets core signal expiry without importing the auth feature
- [ ] `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` -- call the notifier on mid-session `AUTH_EXPIRED` -- the one detection point (AD-2/AD-5)
- [ ] `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart` -- register + wire the notifier into `ApiClient` -- DI
- [ ] `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart` -- add `expired` -- the signal `main.dart` branches on
- [ ] `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart` -- bridge the notifier into `statusStream` -- epic AD, one stream only
- [ ] `lib/features/auth/auth_injection.dart` -- wire the notifier into `SessionRepositoryImpl` -- DI
- [ ] `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` -- add `colorScrim` + any new dialog-card constants -- RNF08
- [ ] `lib/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog.dart` -- new shared overlay component -- UX-DR16/25/27/36
- [ ] `lib/main.dart` -- show/dismiss the overlay across `authenticated`↔`expired` without replacing the screen; add `_BiometricReauthPlaceholder`
- [ ] `test/core/session/session_expiry_notifier_test.dart` -- new -- notify/listen/dispose
- [ ] `test/core/network/api_client_test.dart` -- extend -- notifies only on non-anon-key-function `AUTH_EXPIRED`
- [ ] `test/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl_test.dart` -- extend -- `expired` only fires from `authenticated`
- [ ] `test/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog_test.dart` -- new -- neutral title color, non-dismissible barrier, single-overlay guard, Dynamic Type
- [ ] `test/main_test.dart` -- extend -- overlay appears/dismisses without losing the underlying screen; "Entrar novamente" routes to the placeholder

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the overlay is open, when the user taps the scrim, then nothing happens (barrier is non-dismissible, focus stays trapped on the dialog).
- Given `fvm flutter analyze`, when run after this change, then zero issues and no hardcoded `Color(0x`/`EdgeInsets.*` literal outside `design_tokens.dart`.

## Design Notes

- `colorScrim` must be `Color(0x38241F19)` — `rgba(36,31,25,.22)`, the exact value `cerne-prototype.html` uses for *this* overlay specifically. Its other overlays (drawer, insertion modal, filter/export sheets, account-deletion confirm) use `rgba(36,31,25,.4)` (`0x66...`) instead — don't reuse that heavier value here; it belongs to whichever later story builds those.
- `SessionExpiryNotifier` lives in core (not the auth feature) specifically so `ApiClient` can signal expiry without importing anything from `features/auth` (RNF06) — `SessionRepositoryImpl` is the one bridge back onto the single `SessionStatus` stream.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter pub get` -- resolves, no conflicts
- `fvm flutter test` -- all tests pass
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- zero issues
- `grep -rn "Color(0x\|fontSize:\|EdgeInsets\.\(all\|symmetric\|only\)(" lib/core/session lib/core/network lib/core/widgets lib/features/auth lib/main.dart --include=*.dart` -- expected: no matches outside `design_tokens.dart` (RNF08)

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** `ApiClient._mapDioException` already maps any mid-session `AUTH_EXPIRED` response to `Failure.authExpired` (`api_client.dart:95-111`), but nothing reacts to it — `SessionStatus` only ever emits from the boot-time `restoreSession()` call (`session_repository_impl.dart:81-136`), so an expired session mid-use today surfaces only as a raw inline error on whatever screen made the call, and the user is never routed back to re-auth.

**Approach:** Add a core `SessionExpiryNotifier` port (in the already-scaffolded empty `lib/core/session/`) that `ApiClient` signals on any non-boot `AUTH_EXPIRED`; `SessionRepositoryImpl` bridges that into one new `SessionStatus.expired` value on the epic's existing single stream. `main.dart` keeps rendering the same authenticated screen across that transition and shows a new shared `ConfirmationDialog` overlay (neutral title) whose "Entrar novamente" button routes to a throwaway re-auth placeholder standing in for Epic 2's biometric/PIN flow.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `ApiClient` notifies expiry only for `AUTH_EXPIRED` on calls outside `HeaderInterceptor.anonKeyOnlyFunctions` (`header_interceptor.dart:20-24`, matched via its `functionNameOf`) — boot-time `auth-refresh` keeps going through Story 1.4's existing `restoreSession()` path untouched.
- `SessionStatus` gains exactly one new `expired` value; `statusStream`/`restoreSession`/`dispose` signatures are unchanged — still the epic's one singleton stream (AD), no second stream.
- `SessionRepositoryImpl` emits `expired` only when `_lastStatus == SessionStatus.authenticated`; any other current status ignores the event (no spurious overlay during boot or after logout).
- Overlay = new `ConfirmationDialog` (`lib/core/widgets/`): neutral `colorTextPrimary` title (never `colorError`), non-dismissible barrier, focus-trapped, at most one open at a time (UX-DR16/25/27/36). Entrance is exactly `scrimIn` (0.18s ease-out fade) — the system's only other animation, `sheetUp`, is untouched.
- The authenticated screen's widget instance is never replaced across `authenticated`↔`expired` transitions — scroll/state preserved; the `AuthScreen` branch is unaffected.
- Copy never implies data loss; must state history/scroll position are preserved (mirrors the prototype's own "Sessão expirada" copy).

**Ask First:** if a future consumer needs a session state beyond this story's single new `expired` value, HALT before adding a fourth `SessionStatus` member — renegotiate the epic's AD first.

**Never:**
- No `go_router` — `main.dart` keeps its current `MaterialApp`/`Navigator` shape (Story 1.6).
- No Epic 2 biometric/PIN implementation — "Entrar novamente" only navigates to a throwaway placeholder that Epic 2 deletes wholesale.
- No new icon-font dependency — approximate the prototype's `ph-lock-key` with a built-in Material icon.
- No Reduce-Motion handling — out of this epic's scope.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Mid-session expiry | authenticated, any screen, any endpoint returns `AUTH_EXPIRED` | overlay appears over the current screen; its scroll/state is preserved | silent — no extra inline error |
| Already-open overlay | a second `AUTH_EXPIRED` arrives while the dialog is showing | no second dialog stacks | silent, single-overlay guard holds |
| Expiry while not authenticated | notifier fires but `_lastStatus != authenticated` (e.g. post-logout race) | no emission, no overlay | silent no-op |
| Boot-time refresh expiry | `restoreSession()`'s own `auth-refresh` call returns `AUTH_EXPIRED` | unchanged Story 1.4 behavior — lands on `AuthScreen`, never the overlay | existing path, untouched |
| "Entrar novamente" tapped | overlay visible | dialog dismissed, user routed to the biometric/PIN placeholder | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/core/session/session_expiry_notifier.dart` -- new: `SessionExpiryNotifier` port + broadcast-stream impl, pure Dart (no Flutter/feature import, RNF06) — the directory exists today as a Story 1.1 scaffold (`.gitkeep` only).
- `lib/core/network/api_client.dart:95-111` -- `_mapDioException` additionally calls `SessionExpiryNotifier.notifyExpired()` when the mapped failure `is AuthExpired` and `HeaderInterceptor.functionNameOf(e.requestOptions.path)` isn't in `anonKeyOnlyFunctions` (`header_interceptor.dart:20-24,80-83`) — new constructor dependency.
- `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart:33-61` -- register `SessionExpiryNotifier` as a singleton (with `dispose:`) before `ApiClient`; pass it into `ApiClient`'s constructor.
- `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart` -- add third value `expired` to the current 2-value enum.
- `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart:27-140` -- constructor takes `SessionExpiryNotifier`; subscribes to `expiredEvents`, emits `SessionStatus.expired` per the "Always" guard above; cancels the subscription in `dispose()` (`:139`).
- `lib/features/auth/auth_injection.dart:33-39` -- pass `sessionExpiryNotifier: sl<SessionExpiryNotifier>()` into `SessionRepositoryImpl`.
- `lib/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog.dart` -- new shared component (UX-DR16): scrim + centered card, `titleColor` param (neutral here; Epic 8's account-deletion dialog later passes `colorError`), non-dismissible barrier, single-overlay guard, `scrimIn` entrance.
- `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` -- add `colorScrim` (see Design Notes) plus any new named spacing/padding constants the dialog card needs beyond the existing scale (RNF08).
- `lib/main.dart:90-132` -- `StreamBuilder` treats `authenticated`/`expired` as the same `_PostAuthPlaceholder` render; a small listener shows/dismisses `ConfirmationDialog` on that transition; new throwaway `_BiometricReauthPlaceholder` (same pattern as `_PostAuthPlaceholder`) is "Entrar novamente"'s target.
- Ground truth for copy/visuals: `docs/input/prototype/cerne-prototype.html` ("OVERLAY: Sessão expirada" block) and `prototype-extract.md:69,174-176,227`; `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md:7` (`AUTH_EXPIRED`, 401, non-retryable).

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `lib/core/session/session_expiry_notifier.dart` -- new port + impl -- lets core signal expiry without importing the auth feature
- [ ] `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` -- call the notifier on mid-session `AUTH_EXPIRED` -- the one detection point (AD-2/AD-5)
- [ ] `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart` -- register + wire the notifier into `ApiClient` -- DI
- [ ] `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart` -- add `expired` -- the signal `main.dart` branches on
- [ ] `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart` -- bridge the notifier into `statusStream` -- epic AD, one stream only
- [ ] `lib/features/auth/auth_injection.dart` -- wire the notifier into `SessionRepositoryImpl` -- DI
- [ ] `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` -- add `colorScrim` + any new dialog-card constants -- RNF08
- [ ] `lib/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog.dart` -- new shared overlay component -- UX-DR16/25/27/36
- [ ] `lib/main.dart` -- show/dismiss the overlay across `authenticated`↔`expired` without replacing the screen; add `_BiometricReauthPlaceholder`
- [ ] `test/core/session/session_expiry_notifier_test.dart` -- new -- notify/listen/dispose
- [ ] `test/core/network/api_client_test.dart` -- extend -- notifies only on non-anon-key-function `AUTH_EXPIRED`
- [ ] `test/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl_test.dart` -- extend -- `expired` only fires from `authenticated`
- [ ] `test/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog_test.dart` -- new -- neutral title color, non-dismissible barrier, single-overlay guard, Dynamic Type
- [ ] `test/main_test.dart` -- extend -- overlay appears/dismisses without losing the underlying screen; "Entrar novamente" routes to the placeholder

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the overlay is open, when the user taps the scrim, then nothing happens (barrier is non-dismissible, focus stays trapped on the dialog).
- Given `fvm flutter analyze`, when run after this change, then zero issues and no hardcoded `Color(0x`/`EdgeInsets.*` literal outside `design_tokens.dart`.

## Design Notes

- `colorScrim` must be `Color(0x38241F19)` — `rgba(36,31,25,.22)`, the exact value `cerne-prototype.html` uses for *this* overlay specifically. Its other overlays (drawer, insertion modal, filter/export sheets, account-deletion confirm) use `rgba(36,31,25,.4)` (`0x66...`) instead — don't reuse that heavier value here; it belongs to whichever later story builds those.
- `SessionExpiryNotifier` lives in core (not the auth feature) specifically so `ApiClient` can signal expiry without importing anything from `features/auth` (RNF06) — `SessionRepositoryImpl` is the one bridge back onto the single `SessionStatus` stream.

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter pub get` -- resolves, no conflicts
- `fvm flutter test` -- all tests pass
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- zero issues
- `grep -rn "Color(0x\|fontSize:\|EdgeInsets\.\(all\|symmetric\|only\)(" lib/core/session lib/core/network lib/core/widgets lib/features/auth lib/main.dart --include=*.dart` -- expected: no matches outside `design_tokens.dart` (RNF08)

## Summary — Story 1.5: Expired-Session Recovery Overlay

Spec file: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-5-expired-session-recovery-overlay.md`

**Problem:** `ApiClient` already maps a mid-session `AUTH_EXPIRED` to `Failure.authExpired`, but nothing reacts to it — the `SessionStatus` stream only ever emits from boot-time `restoreSession()`. A session expiring mid-use today just surfaces as an inline error; there's no overlay and no route back to re-auth.

**Approach:**
- New core `SessionExpiryNotifier` port (in the already-scaffolded `lib/core/session/`) lets `ApiClient` signal expiry for any authenticated call's `AUTH_EXPIRED` — excluding the three anon-key-only functions, so boot-time refresh (Story 1.4) is untouched.
- `SessionStatus` gains one new value, `expired`; `SessionRepositoryImpl` bridges the notifier into it, staying on the epic's single mandated stream (no second stream).
- A new shared `ConfirmationDialog` widget renders the scrim + card (neutral title, non-dismissible, single-overlay guard, `scrimIn` 0.18s entrance) — reusable later by Epic 8's destructive-variant dialog.
- `main.dart` keeps the authenticated screen mounted across `authenticated`↔`expired` (never navigates away, preserves scroll/state) and shows/dismisses the dialog on that transition. "Entrar novamente" routes to a throwaway placeholder standing in for Epic 2's biometric/PIN flow.
- One new design token, `colorScrim` (`0x38241F19`, matched exactly to the prototype's own value for *this* overlay — its other overlays use a different, heavier alpha).

**Token count:** ~2,362 (target 900–1600). This is above target because the feature is irreducibly cross-layer for one goal — core networking, core DI, a new core port, a new shared widget, a design token, and app-shell wiring all have to land together for the overlay to function or be testable at all. Kept whole rather than split into artificial, non-shippable pieces.

type: 'feature'
created: '2026-10-28'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
